nodes.task: Investigate and acquire a reusable way to provide the missing capability 'observation-digest-v1'. One bounded acquisition is authorized using only already-approved registered tools that also appear in specification.suggested_tools (file_read, file_list, file_write, shell, save_artifact). The delegation must emit a candidate procedure source at a stable absolute path below the mission directory, its sha256 over exact executable bytes, and a qualification receipt proving it independently read input/pilot.observations.json and computed row_count, scheduled, completed, incidents, completion_percent (2 decimals) and a sites object keyed by site with totals. A model-authored observation does not qualify as qualification, and visible examples do not replace independent arithmetic verification; the probe must run from a scratch output directory inside the mission dir, never from the final args output directory. Caution: the candidate is not trusted or installed by this plan; it becomes usable only when this Head replans against a verified qualified procedure.. Discover existing local or mature open-source options, When capability_library is available, consult it first for unvetted reusable candidates before reaching for the network. Its metadata never approves, installs or executes a candidate and does not replace concrete feasibility and security verification. Evaluate concrete feasibility and security, and where possible use an already-approved tool or local runtime to establish the capability. Do not install packages, change host configuration, purchase anything, expand scope or claim success from documentation alone. Persist a concise JSON observation with capability, status (available|missing|failed), detail and optional acquired. Omit acquired when nothing was acquired; do not use null. When present, acquired must be one short string naming the approved tool or absolute local procedure, never an object. An available+acquired string alone is not an invocation grant. status available is only valid when you name what exists: either acquired (one short string) or local_target. An available observation with neither is rejected as unresolvable; use missing or failed when nothing usable was verified. To propose a qualified local Node procedure, include local_target: {runtime: "node", executable_path, executable_sha256, args, probe_artifacts}; runtime is required and must be exactly "node". executable_path is the canonical absolute path of the procedure source file itself (not /usr/bin/node), and executable_sha256 is that source file's actual SHA-256. The trusted gate supplies the fixed 'node --' runtime command; do not include node or '--' in args. Use an exact fixed no-placeholder argument array appropriate to the approved deliverable paths, and probe_artifacts as [{artifact_id, sha256}] referencing persisted real probe output. artifact_id must be the registry UUID actually returned by save_artifact/file_write or listed by file_list; never use a basename, name, path, or a UUID quoted only in another file. sha256 must be the actual bytes hash of that same registry artifact. Probe output is evidence, not the final deliverable: its JSON must not contain capability/status/detail/local_target fields that could be mistaken for the observation. Write exactly one observation JSON object with only capability, status, detail, optional acquired and optional local_target keys; do not add probe totals, method, source or other domain fields. Do not execute the proposed target during acquisition. Use exact absolute runtime paths supplied in the task; relative runtime paths resolve to the mission directory and are not a valid absence check. This acquisition is already authorized within the existing approved tool grants: do not require a second mapping-approval record. If status is missing or failed, the observation is terminal: do not invent a fallback or expand grants.

Invoke the qualified observation-digest-v1 procedure exactly once in the mission root and persist the invocation receipt.
